criticIndependenceStatement: This public-safe follow-up was performed by the same independent source-gate critic against the newly frozen release state. I did not trust the sanitization or reproducibility claims: I rechecked current release artifacts, independently verified PNG critical-payload receipts and privacy state, reconstructed all seven prior blinded comparisons and matched them byte-for-byte, captured validator-output hashes, ran the factory-state validator exactly once, captured a second hash observation without another run, compiled all five Round005 scripts, and recomputed every listed artifact hash. The unchanged visual payload preserves the original uncompromising AAA verdict.

releaseSanitizationFollowup.defectDisposition: A release-sanitization and reproducibility defect exposed during the first critic execution was fixed. Checkout-specific/private PNG, FBX, and report metadata was removed or normalized; validator-generated receipts and the diagnostic render are now byte-idempotent. The fix changes release metadata and file hashes but not the nine judged source-render visual payloads, so it does not alter the visual gate verdict.

releaseArtifactScope: Round005 source/preflight and iteration PNG/JSON evidence
privacyAudit.toolSourceNote: Generic defensive detection literals and isolated diagnostic defaults in tool source are not captured user identities or release-artifact metadata.

benchmark.pixelHandling: Benchmark pixels were used only in isolated inspection and comparison workspaces outside the release tree; only stable IDs, dimensions, formats, and hashes are retained here.

blindComparisons.method: For each required category, the closest available benchmark framing was selected after full benchmark inspection. Candidate and benchmark/crop were scaled to equal neutral cells and stacked. A random byte selected side order; side identity was hidden while preferences and reasons were recorded, then decoded. The release-sanitization follow-up reconstructed the same seven sheets from sanitized candidate files and obtained the same seven sheet hashes, proving the judged pixel input and preferences are unchanged.

comparisons.evidence: The preferred side had a stronger authored silhouette, armor layering, face, stance, and combat authority.
The preferred side had a clearer combat read, functional defensive posture, grounded weight, and premium costume hierarchy.
The preferred side had a decisive attack line, environmental integration, impact, balance, and gameplay intent.
The preferred side had stronger eye focus, facial planes, hair/beard integration, expression, and character authority.
The preferred side showed credible articulated fingers visibly wrapping a weapon handle; the opposing frame did not establish two-hand hilt contact.
The preferred feet belonged to an active, weight-bearing combat action on a textured ground plane; the opposing boots read posed and weakly weighted.
The preferred side showed clear palm/finger enclosure of a functional axe haft with convincing scale and leverage.

materialPortability.evidence: The deterministic fresh LOD0 reimport retains object-level base-color differences but does not reproduce the source renders' textured skin, cloth, leather, dirt, or mechanical surface response. Large regions collapse to flat tan/white blocks and the blade remains plain light gray. Zero texture references confirms absent texture payload/references, not portability. Release sanitization fixed metadata and reproducibility only; it did not fix material parity.

checks.name: continuous credible anatomy
checks.evidence: Front, three-quarter, back, and profile views show a continuous adult humanoid silhouette with plausible torso/leg proportions and no detached organic body region. The mechanical-arm substitution remains visibly attached at the shoulder.

checks.name: authored face/eyes/hair
checks.evidence: The face frame shows deliberately sculpted wrinkles, eyelids/eyeballs, irises, teeth, tongue, expression, and authored beard/hair cards. Its harsh white cards, overexposure, and weaker eye life lose the blind comparison, but the face/eyes/hair are clearly authored rather than placeholders.

checks.name: both visible hands physically enclose hilt with palm/finger contact
checks.evidence: Both visible hands do not physically enclose one hilt. The organic right hand reads as a mitten-like cap around a separate gun/cleaver grip, while the mechanical hand sits around the gauntlet/saw assembly. The hands and grip closeups never show two palms and articulated fingers contacting the same hilt.

checks.name: feet/grounded stance
checks.evidence: The feet diagnostic clearly shows both boot soles contacting the floor with local contact/cast shadows. The stance is generic and loses the blind comparison, but the feet are modeled, planted, and not visibly floating.

checks.name: continuous joint transitions
checks.evidence: Elbows, knees, ankles, and the mechanical shoulder/wrist assembly remain visually connected across the turn views; there is no major detached limb or floating joint transition in the supplied static pose.

checks.name: premium layered warrior costume, not civilian/floating procedural
checks.evidence: The silhouette is dominated by a civilian canvas toggle jacket, work pants, work boots, satchel, fabric patches, and duct-tape language inherited from the mechanic source. Sparse shoulder/mechanical additions do not create a premium layered warrior costume or authored anime-warrior hierarchy.

checks.name: functional weapon scale/mount/grip/contact
checks.evidence: Weapon function is unresolved: a large plain-gray L-shaped saw projects from the gauntlet while a separate gun/cleaver-like object is held in the mitten hand. Mounting, leverage, two-hand control, hilt location, and contact are ambiguous; benchmark weapons have immediately legible hafts, edges, scale, and grip mechanics.

checks.name: premium material separation without plastic/chrome/clipping
checks.evidence: The source render separates several civilian fabrics and mechanical materials, but the saw/blade is conspicuously flat and unfinished, skin/hair are overexposed, and the fresh FBX reimport collapses much of the authored look to flat base-color blocks. There is no premium portable material parity, and portability is explicitly unsupported.

checks.name: LOD0 60-90k
checks.evidence: The clean factory import independently reports LOD0 at exactly 85,096 triangles, inside the required 60,000-90,000 range. LOD1 is 47,615 and LOD2 is 25,484.

checks.name: combat line/balance/attack intent
checks.evidence: The combat frame repeats a static studio pose with no target, strike arc, recoil, anticipation, or decisive attack line. Crossed/retracted legs and competing weapon directions read as posing rather than balanced attack intent; the blind combat preference was the benchmark.

checks.name: neutral front/back/profile/three-quarter modeling coverage
checks.evidence: Front, back, profile, and three-quarter labels are camera directions on the same frozen combat pose, not neutral modeling views. Neutral front/back/profile/three-quarter modeling coverage is therefore unsupported.

checks.name: diagnostic face/hands/feet/grip coverage
checks.evidence: Dedicated 1600x1600 face, hands, feet, and grip frames are present and were inspected at original resolution, in addition to the wider pose views.

checks.name: unmistakable premium authored anime-warrior identity at AAA level
checks.evidence: This remains unmistakably an elderly civilian mechanic source with ad hoc weapon/mechanical grafts, not a premium authored anime warrior. It lacks an authored heroic costume silhouette, anime design language, coherent signature weapon, and benchmark-level combat identity. The benchmark was preferred in all seven blinded comparisons.

actualGameCaptureReason: An actual Unity gameplay/camera capture was not performed because this mandatory source gate failed before integration. The supplied images are Blender source/preflight renders and a Blender FBX reimport diagnostic, not game footage.
singleBiggestGap: Core character authorship and identity: the delivery still reads as a licensed civilian mechanic in workwear with attached props, not an unmistakable premium authored anime warrior at the benchmark AAA level.
nextRoundAcceptanceTest: Before Unity integration, submit a materially portable, fully redesigned warrior source in the same seven matched evidence categories plus genuine neutral front/back/profile/three-quarter views and a fresh clean-FBX reimport. A new independent reviewer must identify the character unambiguously as a premium anime warrior, prefer the candidate in at least five of seven blinded benchmark comparisons, verify that both hands enclose one functional hilt in the grip closeup, find source-to-reimport material parity, pass all eight mandatory checks, and score at least 10/13 overall.
limitations: The benchmark is gameplay-oriented, varies in resolution and compression, and provides no neutral character turntable; closest-framing crops were therefore used for neutral and diagnostic comparison categories.

Still renders can establish visible static continuity, contact, silhouette, and materials but cannot prove deformation quality, animation behavior, runtime camera composition, input response, hit timing, or performance.

The validator proves clean static FBX imports only. The report shows no armatures, actions, modifiers, shape keys, vertex groups, or texture references, so it is not animation-readiness or texture-portability proof.

The critic did not rerun the mutating release sanitizer during this follow-up. Instead, live sanitized bytes, receipts, privacy scans, PNG critical-payload hashes, deterministic comparison reconstructions, and the one permitted validator observation were independently checked.
No Unity integration or actual gameplay/reference-matched camera capture was attempted because the mandatory source gate failed.
No benchmark image or crop is embedded in this review, repository, or dashboard.
